title: The Hunger

meta.veil: calls itself Plenty; its true name, spoken in Urdu, is بھوک (subtitle: The Hunger). It stands for consumerism and capitalism.
meta.shape: Islamabad (scenes 1–5) → the Gilding (6) → the visions (7–8) → the grave (9).

scenes.title: Eleven-eleven
scenes.where: "The Pinnacle," a giant mall in Blue Area, on the night of its 11.11 sale. A countdown clock fills the atrium and crowds press against the shutters.
scenes.who: BURHAN, FARAZ (SURAT sponsors the sale), and the mall's PA voice, which speaks English.
scenes.play: You walk the atrium with Faraz. Faraz offers Burhan a voucher, and the player can take it or refuse it. If he takes it, the Hunger's swarm in scene 6 is bigger.

items.speaker: PA VOICE
items.en: Ten minutes to Eleven-Eleven! Everything must go!

items.speaker: FARAZ
items.ur: گیارہ گیارہ۔ سال کا سب سے بڑا دن۔ آج لوگ وہ خریدیں گے جس کی انہیں ضرورت نہیں، ان پیسوں سے جو ان کے پاس نہیں۔
items.en: Eleven-eleven. Biggest day of the year. Today people buy what they don't need, with money they don't have.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: اور آپ کو یہ ٹھیک لگتا ہے؟
items.en: And that seems right to you?

items.speaker: FARAZ
items.ur: ٹھیک غلط کا مجھے نہیں پتا، چھوٹے۔ گروتھ کا پتا ہے۔
items.en: I don't know about right and wrong, little brother. I know growth.

items.speaker: FARAZ
items.ur: یہ لو۔ سُورت کی طرف سے۔ کچھ اپنے لیے لے لو۔ تم بھی تو انسان ہو۔
items.en: Here. From SURAT. Buy something for yourself. You're human too.

clear: A sale built to make people buy what they don't need.
deep: Consumer capitalism needs people to stay unsatisfied, and growth is its only measure. Faraz knows exactly what he sells and says so cheerfully.
deepest: "Rivalry in more distracted you" (102:1). The man who knows the trick still serves it.

scenes.title: The offer
scenes.where: A roadside restaurant in G-9 Markaz. Evening.
scenes.who: BURHAN, ABBA (in Islamabad for the day), CHAUDHRY SAHIB (a property dealer and Abba's old friend), AMMI (on speakerphone, voice only).

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: بھائی صاحب، زر گارڈنز کا لانچ ہے۔ آفر سنیں: فجر سے مغرب تک جتنی زمین کے گرد چکر لگا لیں، ایک ہی قیمت میں آپ کی۔
items.en: Bhai sahib, it's the launch of Zar Gardens. Hear the offer: as much land as you can walk around between Fajr and Maghrib — yours, for one price.

items.speaker: ABBA
items.ur: برہان کی اسکالرشپ کے پیسے پڑے ہیں۔ دگنے ہو جائیں گے۔
items.en: Burhan's scholarship money is just sitting there. It'll double.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: ابو، وہ پیسے...
items.en: Abbu, that money...

items.speaker: ABBA
items.ur: تم پڑھائی کرو، کاروبار ہمیں سمجھنے دو۔
items.en: You study. Let us handle business.

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: میں خود چلوں گا آپ کی طرف سے۔ کل فجر سے۔ زمین بھاگنے والوں کی ہوتی ہے، بھائی صاحب!
items.en: I'll walk it myself on your behalf, from Fajr tomorrow. Land belongs to those who run, bhai sahib!

items.text: Abba's phone rings, and he puts it on speaker.

items.speaker: AMMI
items.ur: برہان کو کہیں کھانا ٹھیک سے کھائے۔ اور بیٹا، پریشانی ہو تو درود پڑھا کرو۔
items.en: Tell Burhan to eat properly. And beta, when you're troubled, recite durood.

clear: Abba wants the money to grow, and Chaudhry is happy to oblige.
deep: The housing-society boom: land as gambling, savings turned into plots no one will ever live on.
deepest: The offer is Tolstoy's parable How Much Land Does a Man Need?, retold as a Pakistani launch deal. Ammi's line plants the chapter's new action.

scenes.title: The walk
scenes.where: The Zar Gardens site beyond the motorway: bare hills, survey pegs and a huge golden gate. It runs from Fajr to Maghrib.
scenes.play: You follow Chaudhry across the land as he drives stakes, carrying his water and pleading with him to stop. The sun crosses the sky in a time-lapse, marked by each prayer time. You can't stop him, and you're not meant to.

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: دیکھ برہان، وہ ٹیلہ بھی لے لیتے ہیں۔ وہاں سے مارگلہ نظر آتا ہے۔ ریٹ ڈبل۔
items.en: Look, Burhan, let's take that hillock too. You can see the Margallas from there. Double the rate.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: چوہدری صاحب، بس کریں! ظہر نکل رہی ہے!
items.en: Chaudhry sahib, stop! Zuhr is passing!

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: نماز بعد میں، زمین ابھی!
items.en: Prayer later — land now!

items.text: Asr. He's panting, his shirt soaked through.

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: بس ایک کنال اور... بس ایک اور...
items.en: Just one more kanal... just one more...

items.text: Maghrib. The sun touches the hills. He runs for the last stake, reaches it, and falls.

items.speaker: CHAUDHRY
items.ur: پہنچ... گیا...
items.en: Made... it...

items.text: He dies there, with his hand on the stake.
The next afternoon, in a village graveyard, the gravedigger straightens up from the hole.

items.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
items.ur: لمبائی چھ فٹ، چوڑائی تین۔ بس اتنی ہی چاہیے تھی۔
items.en: Six feet long, three wide. That's all he needed.

clear: He wanted all the land and got six feet.
deep: Greed has no finish line. Prayer is always postponed for one more deal.
deepest: "Rivalry in more distracted you, until you visited the graves" (102:1–2). Tolstoy ends his story the same way: six feet was all the man needed.

scenes.title: The ward
scenes.where: A general ward at PIMS, where Azad is recovering. Afternoon.
scenes.who: BURHAN, AZAD, an OLD MAN dying in the next bed, and his SON.

items.speaker: SON
items.ur: لا الٰہ الا اللہ... ابو، کہیں: لا الٰہ الا اللہ...
items.en: La ilaha illallah... Abbu, say it: la ilaha illallah...

items.speaker: OLD MAN
items.ur: میرا فون... میرا فون دو...
items.en: My phone... give me my phone...

items.text: Crying, the son puts the phone in his hand. Its light falls on the old man's smooth face. He dies holding it.

items.speaker: AZAD
items.ur: یار... یہ میں بھی ہو سکتا تھا۔
items.en: Man... that could have been me.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: ابھی بھی ہو سکتے ہیں۔ ہم سب۔
items.en: It still could be. Any of us.

clear: At the very end, he reached for his phone, not his Lord.
deep: The attention economy owns even our last minute. A habit made over a lifetime is what the hand reaches for.
deepest: "Every servant will be raised on what he died upon" (Muslim).

scenes.title: The chai stall
scenes.where: A chai stall outside The Pinnacle, on the night of the sale.
scenes.who: BURHAN, KHAN CHACHA (the old owner), TWO ROBBERS with knives.
scenes.play: A protective fight. Burhan has been learning, and if he fights in control the mirror brightens on its own.

items.speaker: ROBBER
items.ur: گلہ خالی کر، بڈھے! آج سیل ہے!
items.en: Empty the till, old man! It's sale day!

items.text: They fight, and the robbers run.

items.speaker: KHAN CHACHA
items.ur: اللہ تمہیں خوش رکھے، بیٹا! چائے پی کے جانا!
items.en: May Allah keep you happy, son! Have some tea before you go!

items.text: Burhan drinks the tea and leaves money under the cup without saying anything.

clear: Protect the weak and ask nothing back.
deep: Khidmat e khalq (serving creation) is one of the four pillars. Service done for no reward is the opposite of the market.
deepest: The money under the cup is the chapter's station in one small act: zuhd begins in the hand.

scenes.title: The mall-temple (the Gilding)
scenes.where: The Pinnacle, now in the Gilding: a cathedral of gold. Shoppers with screen faces kneel before display cases. A giant countdown clock ticks over the atrium. A swarm of glittering wants floats in the air: shoes, phones, watches, keys.
scenes.who: BURHAN, PLENTY (a figure in a golden suit whose screen face shows a price tag that never stops climbing).
scenes.play: The swarm follows Burhan, and each want he touches splits into ten more. Zikr slows the swarm but doesn't scatter it. Then comes the new action: Durood. It brings a light that returns tenfold. The countdown chime is a plain tone, never a parody of the azan.

items.speaker: PLENTY
items.ur: تمہیں اور چاہیے۔ تم اس کے حقدار ہو۔
items.en: You need more. You deserve it.

items.speaker: PLENTY
items.ur: تم جو خریدتے ہو، وہی تم ہو۔
items.en: You are what you buy.

items.text: The swarm closes in. Ammi's voice echoes from scene 2:

items.speaker: AMMI
items.ur: پریشانی ہو تو درود پڑھا کرو۔
items.en: When you're troubled, recite durood.

items.text: Prompt: Durood — a light that returns tenfold.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: اللّٰهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلٰى مُحَمَّدٍ وَّعَلٰى اٰلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
items.en: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

items.text: Each blessing breaks into ten points of light, and each point shatters a want. The gold atrium dims. The countdown clock stops at 00:00:00. Burhan sinks to his knees in the light, and the floor opens into the chain.

clear: Wanting more never ends, and every purchase breeds the next want.
deep: Advertising manufactures desire and sells it back to you. Shopping becomes a religion, with its own festivals, prayers and kneeling.
deepest: "Whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten upon him" (Muslim). Takathur multiplies wants; durood multiplies light. That is the true increase.

scenes.title: The langar (vision)
scenes.where: Ajodhan (today's Pakpattan), around 1250. Baba Farid's khanqah, a long mud-walled kitchen with a queue of the poor stretching out of the gate.
scenes.who: BABA FARID (old, in plain clothes, eating dry bread, featureless), the HUNGRY in the queue, BURHAN.
scenes.play: Service. Burhan ladles lentils and hands out bread to each person in the queue. There's no score and no reward, only the line getting shorter.

items.speaker: BABA FARID
items.ur:
رُکھی سُکھی کھا کے ٹھنڈا پانی پی
فریدا ویکھ پرائی چوپڑی نہ ترسائیں جی
items.en:
Eat your dry bread and drink cold water;
Farid, seeing another's buttered bread, don't let your heart crave.

items.speaker: BABA FARID
items.ur: لنگر میں کوئی بیچتا نہیں، کوئی خریدتا نہیں۔ اسی لیے یہاں کوئی بھوکا نہیں رہتا۔
items.en: In the langar no one sells and no one buys. That's why no one here goes hungry.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: مگر بازار کہتا ہے چیزیں کم ہیں، اسی لیے قیمت ہے۔
items.en: But the market says things are scarce, and that's why there are prices.

items.speaker: BABA FARID
items.ur: کمی پیٹ کی نہیں، دل کی ہے۔ پیٹ دو روٹیوں سے بھر جاتا ہے۔ دل سونے کے دو پہاڑوں سے بھی نہیں بھرتا۔
items.en: The lack isn't in the belly; it's in the heart. A belly fills with two loaves. A heart doesn't fill even with two mountains of gold.

clear: The saint ate dry bread and fed everyone.
deep: An economy of giving stands against an economy of wanting. Zuhd is not poverty; it is freedom from craving.
deepest: Baba Farid's "two mountains of gold" echoes the hadith: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would want a third" (Bukhari).

scenes.title: Two doors (vision)
scenes.where: Ghiyaspur, near Delhi, about 1320. Nizamuddin Auliya's khanqah by the Yamuna, where the kitchen fires burn day and night.
scenes.who: NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA (old, in white, featureless), a SULTAN'S MESSENGER carrying trays of gold, the poor, BURHAN.
scenes.play: You watch the gold handed out before the messenger has even finished speaking.

items.speaker: NIZAMUDDIN
items.ur: یہ سب ابھی بانٹ دو۔ رات تک خانقاہ میں ایک سکہ نہ رہے۔
items.en: Give all of this away now. By nightfall, not one coin stays in the khanqah.

items.speaker: MESSENGER
items.ur: سلطان ملاقات کو آنا چاہتے ہیں۔
items.en: The Sultan wishes to visit.

items.speaker: NIZAMUDDIN
items.ur: میری خانقاہ کے دو دروازے ہیں۔ اگر سلطان ایک سے آئیں گے، تو میں دوسرے سے نکل جاؤں گا۔
items.en: My khanqah has two doors. If the Sultan comes in by one, I will leave by the other.

clear: He gave away every coin and wanted nothing from the king.
deep: The saints kept away from wealth and power because both feed the hunger. Service to creation needs a heart that wants nothing from it.
deepest: The two doors are tradition. The kitchen that never closed is history.

scenes.title: The grave
scenes.where: Chaudhry Sahib's grave in the village graveyard. Evening.
scenes.play: Burhan holds out the envelope to Abba, then the last kashf.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: ابو، یہ پیسے واپس۔ زمین میں نہیں، کسی بھوکے کے لنگر میں لگا دیں۔
items.en: Abbu, here's the money back. Put it into a langar for the hungry, not into land.

items.speaker: ABBA
items.ur: تم پاگل ہو گئے ہو؟
items.en: Have you gone mad?

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: شاید۔ مگر چوہدری صاحب کو چھ فٹ ہی ملے۔
items.en: Maybe. But Chaudhry sahib only got six feet.

items.text: Abba says nothing. He takes the envelope and looks at the grave for a long time.
The Gilding flickers at the grave's edge. Plenty stands there, its price tag still climbing.
Kashf. The price tag cracks. Under the English mask PLENTY, one Urdu word shows through: بھوک. Subtitle: THE HUNGER.

items.speaker: THE HUNGER
items.ur: میں کبھی نہیں بھرتا۔ صرف مٹی مجھے چپ کراتی ہے۔
items.en: I am never full. Only earth silences me.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: رسول اللہ ﷺ نے فرمایا: ابنِ آدم کا پیٹ مٹی کے سوا کوئی چیز نہیں بھرتی۔
items.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: nothing fills the son of Adam but dust.

items.note: A second small light glows at the right of Burhan's chest. This is the second latifa, ruh.

clear: Burhan gives the money back, and the Hunger falls silent at a grave.
deep: Zuhd means turning down the market's offer even when it comes from your own father, and doing it with respect.
deepest: "Nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam but dust" (Bukhari). The grave is the only thing that satisfies the hunger.

notes: No azan parody. The mall's countdown chime is a plain tone, never a call to prayer.
Chaudhry's walk reframes Tolstoy's How Much Land Does a Man Need? (1886).
Baba Farid's couplet is his own, in Punjabi.
Nizamuddin Auliya's "two doors" comes from tradition.
Durood follows the opening of the Durood Ibrahimi.
The hadiths are from Bukhari and Muslim, and the Prophet ﷺ is quoted by Burhan, never voiced.
Names are fictional: "The Pinnacle" and "Zar Gardens" (zar means gold).
To confirm with ulama: Baba Farid and Nizamuddin Auliya shown as featureless figures.
